cafehugo.desc: Slow start under the arcades. The corner table I always end up at — order the *tartine* and watch the square wake up.

vosges.desc: A full loop of the arcades, then the garden. My most-shot place in the city — I've never once walked through without stopping.

plates.caption: The tea-room counter under the arcades

carnavalet.desc: A gap in my own archive — I've walked past but never shot it. Added from current visitor notes because it fits the morning and the interest in the city's history.

marche.desc: Lunch standing up. Go to the Moroccan stall at the back — the line looks worse than it is, moves in ten minutes.

rosiers.desc: Falafel in hand, eaten leaning on whatever wall has sun — the line at the green storefront moves faster than it looks.

mouffetard.desc: Buy lunch in pieces down the hill — cheese, bread, a paper cone of fruit — and eat it on the church steps at the bottom.

saintechapelle.sub: Île de la Cité · timed entry
saintechapelle.desc: I've never gotten a shot here worth keeping — always too crowded. One clean reference image from the web; book the 2pm slot to beat the afternoon queue.

berthillon.desc: The one I've come back to most. Get the *salted-caramel* and eat it walking the quai — the whole island is the point.

prov.walkNote: measured from EXIF gaps across 5 separate visits, not estimated

tournelle.desc: The bridge between the two islands — look west and the river opens up with Notre-Dame behind you. My own frame is a midday one, high summer.

luxembourg.sub: grab a green chair by the pond
luxembourg.desc: The chairs by the octagonal pond are the whole point — drag one to face the palace and stay longer than you planned.

shakespeare.desc: Go upstairs to the reading room and actually sit down — the front is a scrum, the top floor is quiet.

tenbelles.sub: 10 Rue de la Grange aux Belles
tenbelles.desc: Flat white to go, then straight down to the water — this whole morning is meant to be walked with a cup in hand.

canal.desc: Cross every footbridge you come to — the arched green ones frame the water perfectly, and a lock or two usually opens mid-morning.

sacre.sub: the steps, not the summit crowd
sacre.desc: Sit on the steps below the basilica facing out — the view down over the city beats the one from the very top. Come up the hill on foot rather than the funicular; the climb is half of it.

plates.caption: From a window across the hill
Fête de la Musique on the steps
High summer, looking down the hill

prov.walkNote: six visits across nine years — the steps, in every season I have

pere.sub: enter at the Gambetta gate, walk down
pere.desc: Come in high and let gravity carry you downhill through the oldest section — the cobbled avenues under the planes are the reason to come, not the famous graves.

aligre.desc: Two markets in one — the rowdy open-air street and the calm covered hall behind it. Do the street first, coffee in the hall after.

chezjanou.desc: Provençal dinner two streets off the square — book the early seating; the pastis list alone is worth the walk.

baronrouge.desc: Never shot it — added from web notes. A glass and a plate of oysters at a barrel out front; cash is easiest.

notredame.desc: Go early — the parvis before nine is almost private. Inside, the stone is *pale again* since the reopening; I finally have interior shots worth keeping.

prov.walkNote: shot across five visits, before and after the reopening

vertgalant.sub: the point of the Île de la Cité
vertgalant.desc: Down the steps behind the Pont Neuf statue — the prow of the island, water on both sides. Face west and let the boats slide past.

plates.caption: The point, from the Pont des Arts

pontdesarts.desc: Come at dusk with something to drink and sit on the quai below — the Institut dome goes gold and there is always a busker mid-span.

louvre.desc: The courtyard is the visit — pyramid, Louis XIV on his horse, and the long façades. Save the galleries for a rainy day; the cour costs nothing.

pompidou.desc: The inside-out building, currently wrapped for its long renovation — which is its own kind of honest: pipes on pipes. The plateau out front still earns the detour.

stgermain.desc: One coffee, two terraces — pick whichever corner has sun. In December the whole crossroads strings itself in lights.

alexiii.desc: Cross it at last light — the Grand Palais roof and the gilded horses catch fire, and the tower shows up small and silhouetted downstream.

arc.sub: climb it — the view beats the tower’s
arc.desc: The rooftop is the best viewpoint in Paris *because the tower is in it*. Twelve avenues below, and the Champs running straight back down.

plates.caption: Street level, Place Charles de Gaulle
From the top, toward La Défense

eiffel.sub: Trocadéro, at the hour it goes gold
eiffel.desc: Skip the queue, keep the view: the Trocadéro terrace at dusk, then walk down through the gardens and stand under it when the lights come on.

plates.caption: Night, from the foot of the tower
From a side street in the 7e

prov.walkNote: six visits — dusk is the reliable one

orsay.desc: The single big commitment of the day — and it belongs to the morning, before the queues thicken and while the top-floor light is still soft on the paintings. Orsay was a railway station before it was a museum, so the whole collection sits beneath a vaulted glass roof and a giant station clock: Monet and the water-lily years, Degas’ dancers, the Van Gogh room, Renoir’s crowds — the founding hits of Impressionism, all in a couple of unhurried hours. Take it first, and everything the day does afterward — the gardens, the bookshop, the river at dusk — is downhill, on foot, and completely unrushed.

maisonrose.sub: Rue de l’Abreuvoir · the pink corner
maisonrose.desc: The pink house on the bend, two minutes off the crush at Place du Tertre — and the lane behind it empties out completely. Worth the detour on the way down from the basilica.

hibou.desc: The owl café on the Odéon crossroads — rattan chairs shoulder to shoulder and a crème that arrives on its own branded coaster. Better people-watching than the famous terraces ten minutes west.

buci.desc: The Saint-Germain corner that never quite closes — market stalls in the morning, waiters threading the terraces by seven.

preauxclercs.desc: A proper corner brasserie two streets from the river — white awning, rattan chairs, and a terrace that catches the late-morning sun on the Bonaparte side.

debauve.desc: Chocolatier since 1800 in a listed shopfront — coupes of ganaches under glass, each tray with its own name-card. Buy the Saint-Pères pralinés; the box outlasts the trip.

atlas.desc: Moules in a copper pot on the terrace at Maubert — a carafe of red, mustard on the table, the 5e going past. Order the frites separately and share nothing.

amelie.desc: Maison Collignon — the green-fronted épicerie from *Amélie*, still trading under its film-set sign on the walk up to the basilica. Fruit crates out front, exactly as shot.

plates.caption: Maison Collignon, as in the film

seinecruise.desc: The one tourist ritual worth the ticket — an evening departure, the city going gold from water level, every bridge a ceiling as you pass under it. Take the sunset slot if you can get it.

stpaul.desc: Linked courtyards of antique dealers off Rue Saint-Antoine — and the corner bakery by the métro where I pick up breakfast before the browse.
